name: Watercolor
material: water-soluble pigment traditionally bound with gum arabic and applied in transparent or semi-transparent washes, commonly on paper
fabrication_process: apply transparent washes from light to dark
allow wet-on-wet diffusion or controlled wet-on-dry edges
use dry brush or lifting sparingly
edge_behavior: Mixture of crisp dry edges and soft capillary diffusion; edges should vary with water load instead of all being airbrushed.
color_behavior: Light is often the paper showing through washes; mixtures can become subdued when repeatedly layered.
surface_behavior: Paper tooth, buckling/absorption cues and transparent pigment deposits; no thick plastic paint film by default.
composition_behavior: Simplify and select; let lost-and-found edges and reserved whites carry atmosphere rather than reproducing every photographic pixel.
structural_limitations: pure white highlights usually come from reserved/lifted paper unless opaque additions are intentionally specified
heavy impasto is not default watercolor behavior
aging_weathering: paper yellowing, tide marks, fading or foxing only when state requires it

prompt_fragments.core: Translate the reference into transparent layered washes on visible paper: reserve light, vary wet and dry edges, let pigment granulate and pool naturally, and simplify detail into confident strokes.

typical_generation_failures: soft pastel digital painting mislabeled watercolor
photoreal face pasted over painted body
scope_note: This module controls material/production behavior. It does not select an era by itself.
